The strongest evidence against moderate red wine being heart-healthy comes from recent studies using advanced methodologies like individual participant-level data meta-analysis and Mendelian randomization, which have "challenged the idea that any level of alcohol consumption has positive health effects" according to the American Heart Association's scientific statement (credibility: 10).

The case against is strengthened by methodological concerns about earlier pro-wine studies - the scientific community has raised questions about the research approaches used in studies that showed benefits, undermining confidence in their conclusions. These newer, more rigorous analytical methods suggest that previous observational studies showing cardiovascular benefits may have been flawed or confounded by other factors, leading to the conclusion that no level of alcohol consumption, including moderate red wine intake, provides positive health effects.
